Friday 21st August’s issue is presented by CodeRabbit

Review The Actual Change, Not The File List

AI writes more code than ever. Reviewing it shouldn’t mean scrolling forty files in alphabetical order.

CodeRabbit Review reorganizes any pull request from a flat file list into a structured, layer-by-layer walkthrough - the logical reading order of the change, not the order your platform happens to sort it.

Every range gets its own plain-language summary, with sequence diagrams, state machines, and ERDs generated inline wherever a visual earns its place.

  • Cohorts group related files and chunks so you review one idea at a time.

  • Layers order them so foundational changes - data shapes, contracts - come before the code that depends on them.

  • Code Peek lets you click any variable, function, class or type to see its definition and usages without leaving the tab.

  • Semantic Diff cuts past formatting noise to show what actually changed.

From the team that pioneered AI code reviews. 2M reviews every week. 6M repos. 15K customers. Free during early access.

Review Your Next PR With CodeRabbit Review Today

 

Revised Rules Of Engineering Leadership

— Will Larson

tl;dr: “This post documents the new rules I’ve revised my approach to engineering leadership around, and then talks through the specific projects I’ve worked on over the past year that caused me to believe in these rules.”

Leadership Management
 

You're Not Bad At Hard Things

— Steve Huynh

tl;dr: “Confusing hard and difficult is an issue. Why? Because the two types of problems should be handled in opposite ways. When something is hard, putting in more effort is the right move. When something is complex, more effort will merely compound the problem.”

CareerGrowth DecisionMaking

(4) Semantic Diff cuts past formatting noise to show what actually changed. From the team that pioneered AI code reviews. 2M reviews every week. 6M repos. 15K customers. Free during early access.

Promoted by CodeRabbit

Tools+Setup AI CodeReview
 

How Should Engineering Leaders Measure The ROI Of AI?

— Lizzie Matusov

tl;dr: “Most engineering leaders can name usage stats for their AI tools. Far fewer engineering leaders can quantify the value they got. The distance between those two numbers is creating friction as AI costs skyrocket, so this week we ask: how should engineering leaders measure the ROI of AI?”

Leadership Metrics AI

“You get in life what you have the courage to ask for.”

 
― Nancy D. Solomon

Headed For The Exit: The Great Engineering Leader Career Break

— Gergely Orosz

tl;dr: “To find out what might be behind this spate of sign-outs, I talked with almost 20 engineering leaders currently on a career break – or seriously considering one – and they let me into their personal reasons for deciding to jam the brakes on their careers.”

Leadership Wellbeing CareerGrowth
 

You're Not Short Of Opportunities. You're Short Of The Right Ones.

tl;dr: Dex is the AI talent agent for Software Engineers. Brief Dex once on your stack and what you'd actually move for, and it comes back with vetted Series A+ roles with salary attached: a £100k floor, £150k median, plus a direct intro to the hiring manager. No CV, no recruiter reselling your details, no process you didn't ask to be in.

Promoted by Dex

CareerGrowth Hiring
 

My Development Setup In 2026

— Brandon Weaver

tl;dr: “As I start to step into another new adventure I took a long hard look at my development setup on my work laptop as well as my home laptop and realized I haven’t really cleaned it up in what, a decade now? It was time for some spring cleaning to get it under control and start asking hard questions about what added value and what had somehow smuggled its way across migrations over the past decade. This post explores some of my setup, why I made certain decisions, and how I’m different now than I was back then.”

Tools+Setup
 

Curl Performance

— Daniel Stenberg

tl;dr: “How fast is “fast” and is it good enough? Does it run as fast now as it did before or was there a regression? What exactly needs to be fast? How fast is it? These are questions that many projects and products face, and in curl we are no different.”

OpenSource Performance
 

Baking A Model

— Kent Beck

tl;dr: “I feel the same way about AI models right now. I don’t claim to understand the details, not yet, but I’m fascinated by the mechanism of it all. I’m interested in both: How models work but also, the machinery that makes a model. It’s this latter topic, how a model gets constructed, that I will begin to explore in this post.”

AI DeepDive
 

Null Pointer

Quick Stand-up

Hand-drawn by Manu. View the Null Pointer series.
